title: Deligne's "Hodge Theory I, II, and III"
Hodge Theory I
text:
We intend to give a heuristic dictionary between statements in \ell-adic cohomology and statements in Hodge theory. This dictionary has as its most notable sources (Serre 1960) and the conjectural theory of Grothendieck motives (Demazure 1969). Up until this point, it has mainly served to formulate conjectures in Hodge theory, and it has sometimes even suggested a proof.

1

A mixed Hodge structure H consists of

a \ZZ-module H_\ZZ of finite type (the “integer lattice”);
a finite increasing filtration W of H_\QQ=H_\ZZ\otimes\QQ (the “weight filtration”);
a finite decreasing filtration F of H_\CC=H_\ZZ\otimes\CC (the “Hodge filtration”).

This data is subject to the following condition: there exists a (unique) bigradation of \Gr_W(H_\CC) by subspaces H^{p,q} such that

\Gr_W^n(H_\CC)=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}
the filtration F induces on \Gr_W(H_\CC) the filtration 
  \Gr_W(F)^p
  = \bigoplus_{p'\geq p} H^{p',q'}

\overline{H^{pq}}=H^{qp}.


A morphism f\colon H\to H' is a homomorphism f_\ZZ\colon H_\ZZ\to H'_\ZZ such that f_\QQ\colon H_\QQ\to H'_\QQ and f_\CC\colon H_\CC\to H'_\CC are compatible with the filtrations W and F (respectively).
The Hodge numbers of H are the integers 
  h^{pq} = \dim H^{pq} = h^{qp}.
\tag{1.2}
\tag{1}
We say that H is pure of weight n if h^{pq}=0 for p+q\neq n (i.e. if \Gr_W^i(H)=0 for i\neq n). We also say that H is a Hodge structure of weight $n}.
The Tate Hodge structure \ZZ(1) is the Hodge structure of weight -2, of pure degree (-1,-1), for which \ZZ(1)_\CC=\CC and \ZZ(1)_\ZZ = 2\pi i\ZZ = \Ker(\exp\colon\CC\to\CC^*)\subset\CC. We set \ZZ(n)=\ZZ(1)^{\otimes n}.
We can show that mixed Hodge structures form an abelian category. If f\colon H\to H' is a morphism, then f_\QQ and f_\CC are strictly compatible with the filtrations W and F (cf. [Hodge Theory II, 2.3.5]).








Bibliography

Demazure, M. 1969. “Motifs Des Variétés Algébriques.” Sém. Bourbaki, Talk no. 365.


Serre, J.-P. 1960. “Analogues Kählériens de Certaines Conjectures de Weil.” Ann. Of Math. 71: 392–94.
